title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: CircleCI
providers.scope_notes: Covers CircleCI Cloud. CircleCI cloud (Free, Performance, Scale); SAML SSO and audit log streaming need Scale, context security-group restrictions only on github-type orgs; CircleCI Server is out of scope.

controls.name: Context restrictions (security group, project, expression)
controls.what: Limit which users, projects and pipeline conditions can use a context.

controls_unknown: Any org-admin setting to block, list or revoke members' personal API tokens.
Any org setting to disable OAuth Dynamic Client Registration tokens.
Any inbound IP allowlist for the CircleCI API or web app.
Whether personal API token create/delete or API reads appear in audit logs (not in the published event list).
Whether an SSO-authorized token stops working when the IdP session ends or the user is removed from the IdP.

auth_paths.name: Contexts and project environment variables (stored secrets)

authentication.summary: Third-party secrets stored in CircleCI and injected into jobs. The API returns only names or masked values; the realistic way to read them is to run a job that uses them.

ip_restriction.boundary: The target system enforces network rules. With the IP ranges feature (Performance or Scale), job traffic comes from published CircleCI ranges that the target can allowlist.

renewal.summary: Rotate at source and update the variable.

administration.summary: Any org member can create contexts; contexts default to 'All members'. Admins can add security-group (github orgs only), project and expression restrictions, which combine with AND. Org admins have unrestricted context access.
administration.conditions: Security group restrictions only for github-type orgs.

offboard.details: Secrets belong to the context or project. To use a context, the actor running the workflow must be an org member with access to the context.

inventory.details: GET /context and GET /context/{context_id}/environment-variable, GET /project/{project-slug}/envvar, and the CircleCI Environment Inspector list variable names (values are masked).

network.ui: In .circleci/config.yml set circleci_ip_ranges: true on the job; allowlist jobs.knownips.circleci.com ranges at the target

usage.ui: Org > Security > Audit Logs > Request audit logs (CSV); filter action context.secrets.accessed, target = context

log_sources.name: CircleCI audit logs
log_sources.notes: context and env var change events; context.secrets.accessed.

anomaly_cues: Context accessed by a new project or branch
Masking bypass in step output (base64, reformatting)

containment.steps: Block new work, rotate the secret at its source, update the variable, add context restrictions.
containment.notes: Leaked values stay valid until rotated at the issuing system.

evidence.title: Pause or stop pipelines during an incident
Restrict your pipeline traffic to specific IP ranges
